reviews.title: Not worth it, app for a paid monthly “news”subscription with too many issues for basic functionality
reviews.text: Frustrating app to encapsulate News. Lands in the middle of news feeds requiring scrolling up to start reading news. It doesn’t manage where it is in the news feeds, often flipping back to something you read earlier. It cannot manage conversation threads in the comments section. If you comment and someone replies, then you reply to their comment, your reply should show under their comment and so on. It doesn’t - it posts it as a reply to your original comment. What a mess, that is basic functionality like an email conversation thread behaves but this can’t. It also terminates your in-edit comments at a set number of characters, but when you post your comment the termination occurs way before so your posted comment looks like it is cut off. These are basic bugs that should have been caught before release.

reviews.title: Do Better DM
reviews.text: I downloaded this app as the Daily Mail website became so inundated with glitches and bugs. Unfortunately, I didn't realize that the app was just as bad as the website. I have had multiple instances of being redirected to advertisements that I was scrolling past while reading articles, stories that will not load, and many times I can't even access the app at all. The most annoying glitch I have noticed, however, is that my comments will not post. This is not due to my comments going against the house rules, but because of a "technical issue" according to Daily Mail. I have contacted Daily Mail multiple times about the app not posting my comments. To my dismay, every time I attempt to speak to a customer service rep, I am connected to a rep by the name of "Jordan" who I now know is an AI assistant. "Jordan" always tells me that it's an unfortunate bug, however, doesn't give me any information on how to fix it. This issue seemed to get worse after I updated the app, shocker. This glitch is especially annoying as it has also made it impossible for me to flag inappropriate comments as well. It is incredibly frustrating when I can't post a comment that abides by the house rules, yet I read terribly inappropriate comments from other DM users that I am not permitted to flag. I have made sure that my account is active and I don't have any restrictions on it either and I still can't post comments, sadly Daily Mail doesn't seem to be concerned about this issue.

reviews.title: Drained my battery
reviews.text: I have a month old iPhone 17 Pro, I have been using this app for many years and while it had its faults with glitches, this one was a step too far. My battery lasts a very long time, usually only charge it once every 1-2 days. I read in bed before I go to sleep. I fell asleep reading an article like I do a lot, I woke up two hours before my alarm was due to go off for work and my phone was completely flat. It had 78% when I was reading the app a few hours prior. Upon checking my battery usage data it showed that the daily mail app had used 56% of my battery usage that day, and it was the app running in the background while I was asleep that made the battery die. The graph even showed the battery drainage being much quicker than usual. This isn’t acceptable, there is no reason why a news app should use up so much storage or battery life on your phone. It’s a good job I woke up when I did otherwise my alarm for work wouldn’t have gone off. It just meant I was extra tired that day. If this happens again I will be abandoning the app for good.

Dear editor, please consider these aspects and redesign or re-introduce the old style newspaper look. Until then I’m looking for my news elsewhere online.
